In recent fiscal 2025 quarterly results, top-line revenue has advanced at a mid-to-high single-digit pace, led by the Cloud Intelligence Group, where revenue growth accelerated year-over-year propelled by triple-digit expansion in AI-related product demand and widespread adoption of open-source Qwen foundation models that continued into 2026.

This capital intensity, combined with continued operating losses in cross-border commerce, pushed free cash flow into substantial quarterly deficits in recent 2025 and 2026 filings. While Alibaba preserves an extraordinary liquidity cushion of $69,933.0M in liquid cash and investments against $39,281.0M in debt ($30,652M net cash, or $12.69 per share), distributable cash flow to equity owners has been severely curtailed by this infrastructure cycle.

Furthermore, aggressive across-the-board price cuts in public cloud instances and multi-billion-dollar quarterly cash drains in international cross-border retail suggest that Alibaba is running on an expensive defensive treadmill, spending vast sums simply to maintain market share rather than compounding excess economic profit.

How Things Are Going Now

Operationally, across fiscal 2025 and heading into fiscal 2026, Alibaba is generating an annualized revenue run-rate of $158,556.0M with a consolidated gross margin of 38.2%, supported by a dense active merchant ecosystem, over 42 million 88VIP premium loyalty members, and accelerating enterprise cloud compute workloads. In recent fiscal 2025 quarterly results, top-line revenue has advanced at a mid-to-high single-digit pace, led by the Cloud Intelligence Group, where revenue growth accelerated year-over-year propelled by triple-digit expansion in AI-related product demand and widespread adoption of open-source Qwen foundation models that continued into 2026.

However, these 2025 and early 2026 results confirm that top-line stability masks severe profit and cash flow dilution. Consolidated operating margins have faced steep pressure as management deliberately allocated capital toward user acquisition, price-matching subsidies, instant quick-commerce logistics, and aggressive enterprise cloud discounting. Customer Management Revenue within domestic e-commerce grew at only low single digits through fiscal 2025 as transactions gravitated toward lower-margin Taobao merchants, forcing management to introduce a basic 0.6% software fee while waiving legacy annual fees to stem merchant defections.

Most critically, capital expenditures across fiscal 2025 and the 2026 outlook have escalated dramatically to fund the buildout of generative AI data centers and custom compute infrastructure, reaching multi-billion-dollar quarterly run-rates. This capital intensity, combined with continued operating losses in cross-border commerce, pushed free cash flow into substantial quarterly deficits in recent 2025 and 2026 filings. While Alibaba preserves an extraordinary liquidity cushion of $69,933.0M in liquid cash and investments against $39,281.0M in debt ($30,652M net cash, or $12.69 per share), distributable cash flow to equity owners has been severely curtailed by this infrastructure cycle.
